trickyParts: `command -v jq` in the harness bash answers for its builtin (prints `jq`, exit 0, on an image with no /usr/bin/jq), so every PATH check is a subprocess form: `bash -c 'type -P jq ssh-keygen'`, `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin sh -c 'command -v …'`, `/usr/bin/env jq --version`, `test -x`. Inside the chroot's dash, `command -v jq ssh-keygen` prints only the first name; `type -P` under bash prints both.

Under gVisor a plain `mount --bind /dev <rootfs>/dev` is refused (`wrong fs type`), `mount --rbind /dev <rootfs>/dev` works; without it the probe fails at `open /dev/null` and ssh-keygen at `Couldn't open /dev/null`.
Debian trixie's jq 1.7.1-6+deb13u4 prints `jq-1.7` for `--version`, not `jq-1.7.1`.

The previous image run's log does contain one `Setting up jq`: the plugin build stage installs jq for the omp.extensions rewrite (line ~116) and never reaches the runtime image; the runtime-stage lines are the ones that distinguish before and after.
The second Worker Image run reused the runtime apt layer from the first (CACHED), so the apt `Setting up` lines are in run 38765120996's log, the toolchain step and probe in 38766268187's.
